personality_one_liner: A premium, editorial-style bakery companion balancing the warm, rustic soul of French artisanship with clean, modern utility.

spacing.rule: Generous magazine-like vertical rhythms. Elements should breathe heavily. Intentional whitespace over crammed cards.

do's: Use over hero recipe image for title/metadata overlays.
Use for sticky tab bars if content scrolls underneath.
Pair with >70% surfaceInverse tint underneath when applying text to guarantee readability.
dont's: Avoid on form inputs or dense text areas.
Do not use on regular recipe list cards (use flat surfaceSecondary instead).

screens.name: Accueil (Home)
screens.purpose: Editorially curated discovery feed for recipes and tips.

states.loading: Centered minimal spinner with 'Préparation du four...'
states.empty: Illustration of flour dusting, 'Aucune recette à l\'affiche.'
states.error: Error message with a retry button 'Relancer'.

screens.layout: NYT Cooking style layout. Start with a massive hero recipe card (image filling width, gradient scrim bottom, title in Cormorant). Followed by horizontal scrolling sections: 'Astuces du jour' (Tip of the day) and 'Grands Classiques' (Baguette, Croissant).

screens.name: Recettes (Library)
screens.purpose: Browse and filter the ~20 classic French bakery recipes.

states.empty: Illustration of an empty bread basket.

screens.layout: Sticky top horizontal scroll for category chips (Pains, Viennoiseries, Pâtes). Underneath, a clean 2-column grid of recipe cards. Cards have square images, elegant titles below (no borders, no shadows).

screens.name: Recipe Detail
screens.purpose: Step-by-step cooking guide with hydration/fermentation data.

states.loading: Skeleton loader for image and text blocks.

screens.layout: Large hero image at the top. Back button in a glass FAB. Below image: Title, Author, Difficulty, Time. Then a sticky Segmented Control (Ingrédients / Préparation). In Ingrédients: clean checklist format. In Préparation: numbered steps with bold headers.

screens.name: Assistant IA
screens.purpose: Claude Sonnet 5 powered chat for technical baking questions.
screens.layout: Clean chat interface. AI bubbles in surfaceSecondary, user bubbles in brandTertiary. Input field at bottom pinned to keyboard, using subtle borders instead of heavy input boxes.

screens.name: Share Recipe
screens.purpose: Form to upload personal recipes (photo, ingredients, steps).
screens.layout: Single column form inside KeyboardAvoidingView. Minimalist inputs with labels above. Large dotted-border area for photo upload. Sticky 'Publier' CTA button at the bottom.

screens.name: Profil
screens.purpose: Identity card: who the baker is (avatar, bio, Instagram), their standing (stats, level/XP progression, badges), and their published work (recipes, creations, comments) — plus a link to their professional Team.

states.empty: 'Vous n\'avez pas encore partagé de recette.'

screens.layout: Editorial header with user avatar (or initials), name, @username, bio and Instagram link. Horizontal stats row (recipes, comments, likes, followers, following). Level/XP progression card. Badges preview row linking to the full badge collection. 'Mes créations' gallery (up to 6, with a link to the rest). Team preview (up to 6 members, with a link to the rest). Below that, three tabs: 'Mes recettes', 'Sauvegardées', 'Mes commentaires'. Settings accessible via a subtle gear icon in the header; Amis/Abonnements/Classement/Messagerie/Collections/Mes badges are reached from the Profil tab's own menu, not from this screen.

instructions_to_main_agent: Follow the 'Editorial Mobile LIGHT' layout deeply. Minimal borders, no drop shadows (shadow_tier: 0). Rely on generous padding and typography sizes to establish hierarchy.
Ensure 'Cormorant Garamond' is used for headings and 'Geist' or a similar highly legible sans-serif for body copy and UI elements (buttons, chips). Cap font weights at 500.

Whenever applying text over images (e.g., hero recipe cards), you MUST apply the gradient-to-dark scrim pattern (bottom stop opacity ≥70% of surfaceInverse) behind the text to ensure WCAG AA contrast.
For the recipe detail view, mimic NYT Cooking's split tab behavior for Ingredients vs Preparation, so the UI remains uncluttered.
Keep color usage strictly within the defined warm artisanal palette. Absolutely NO blue, purple, or indigo tokens. Use the rust-orange 'brand' (#C05A35) for primary calls to action.
